resources.string: Takes screenshots when you trigger them (Quick Tap or the Quick Settings tile) and keeps them in memory until you choose to save, copy, or share. It does not read screen content, keystrokes, or gestures.
Stock Pixel only (GrapheneOS/AOSP don’t ship Quick Tap): Settings → System → Gestures → Quick Tap → Open app → LibreShot
Double-tap the back of the phone. Uses the accelerometer only while the screen is on.
Double-press Volume Down to capture. Swallows volume presses while on. Re-enable the accessibility service after changing.
Off = open the editor straight after capture
Privacy: no network permission, no analytics. Screenshots live in memory until you save, copy, or share. The optional back-tap trigger reads the accelerometer only while the screen is on.
iOS-style screenshots: peek, edit, copy, gone.

LibreShot uses Android’s accessibility screenshot API because it’s the only way to take a screenshot without saving a file. The service does not read screen content, does not see your keystrokes, and only acts when you trigger a capture.
Settings → System → Gestures → Quick Tap → Open app → LibreShot. Double-tap the back of the phone to capture.
This build has no Quick Tap gesture. Instead: enable “Back-tap capture” in LibreShot settings, add the LibreShot tile to Quick Settings, or use the volume-down double-press.

This device has no Quick Tap gesture. Instead: enable “Back-tap capture” in LibreShot settings, add the LibreShot tile to Quick Settings, use the volume-down double-press, or set the side key’s double-press to open LibreShot (Settings → Advanced features → Side key).
Capture with a tap, peek at a corner thumbnail, mark it up, then copy or save. Nothing touches your gallery unless you choose Save.
Optional extras live in Settings: back-tap capture, the volume-down capture chord, thumbnail duration and corner, and haptics.
